facts.text: The README limits this package to Gazebo simulation of low-level torque, position and angular velocity control and says Gazebo cannot do high-level walking; physical robots use the separate unitree_ros_to_real project.
normal.launch spawns the twelve A1 joint controllers under the /a1_gazebo namespace.
servo.cpp subscribes to the twelve /<robot>_gazebo/<joint>_controller/state MotorState topics and to /trunk_imu and the four /visual/*_foot_contact/the_force topics.
UnitreeJointController subscribes to the relative command topic and publishes the relative state topic with a realtime publisher.
The controller's update loop reads command.readFromRT() on every cycle, so the last MotorCmd continues to be applied until another command replaces it.
BRAKE mode sets zero position stiffness, zero velocity, damping 20 and zero torque; it is a damping command, not an acknowledged stop of the controller or the Gazebo world.
UnitreeJointController::stopping() has an empty body; the controller lifecycle reports no stop action.
The MotorCmd and MotorState message types are included from the unitree_legged_msgs package by the joint-controller header.
The A1 URDF states revolute position, velocity and effort limits for the twelve leg joints.
The aggregate /<robot>_gazebo/lowState/state LowState publisher is created in the servo main loop.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording fake with no physics step, no controller update loop and no pacing; canned LowState values do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers the twelve command topics and the aggregate LowState subscription declared here and runs no ROS graph, controller, Gazebo physics or contact
the LowState values are placeholders; a live deployment must receive them from the operator's unitree_servo and Gazebo graph
the twelve command publications are independent topics, not one atomic twelve-joint action; a publish receipt proves only that rosbridge accepted the message
no native stop is bound and the last MotorCmd persists in the controller's realtime buffer, so the runtime latch cannot stop the simulated physics
the upstream package has no acknowledged stop service or action and no hardware interface at this pin; physical control is a separate unitree_ros_to_real deployment
position and damping gains are operator-required because no pinned text states a device gain bound

safe_state.description: No native stop is bound. The runtime latch refuses further commands, but each UnitreeJointController keeps applying the last MotorCmd from its RealtimeBuffer and the Gazebo world continues to step; a BRAKE MotorCmd is a damping command on one command topic and is not an acknowledged stop.
